text: Which among the following purification methods is based on the principle of "Solubility" in two different solvents?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The purification method among the ones listed that is based on the principle of "Solubility" in two different solvents is Option D, Differential Extraction.

Differential extraction, also known as liquid-liquid extraction or solvent extraction, is a technique to separate compounds based on their relative solubilities in two different immiscible liquids, usually water and an organic solvent. It exploits the fact that the compound of interest has different solubility properties in two solvents which are not miscible with each other. A solution containing the desired compound and impurities is mixed with a second solvent in which the desired compound is more soluble. The two solvents form layers due to their immiscibility, and the compound partitions into the layer where it is more soluble. By separating the layers and repeating the process if necessary, a higher degree of purification can be achieved for the target compound.

Let's quickly review why the other options do not primarily use solubility in two different solvents:

Distillation (Option A): Distillation is a process that separates the components of a mixture based on differences in their boiling points. It does not rely on differential solubility in two solvents.

Sublimation (Option B): Sublimation is the phase transition of a substance from the solid to the gas phase without passing through the intermediate liquid phase. This process is based on the volatility of the substance, not on its solubility in solvents.

Column Chromatography (Option C): Column chromatography separates compounds based on their differing affinities to a stationary phase (often a solid) and a mobile phase (often a liquid). The separation is achieved by partitioning between the phases, but it does not primarily involve the solubility of the compounds in two different immiscible solvents.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Evening Shift

text: The solution from the following with highest depression in freezing point/lowest freezing point is
options: $180\mathrm{g}$ of acetic acid dissolved in benzene
$180\mathrm{g}$ of acetic acid dissolved in water
$180\mathrm{g}$ of benzoic acid dissolved in benzene
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Depression in freezing point ($\Delta T_{f}$) is a colligative property. This means its value depends directly on the effective number of solute particles present in the solution. The formula we use for this is:

$\Delta T_{f}=i\cdot K_{f}\cdot m$

Here, $i$ is the van 't Hoff factor, $K_{f}$ is the molal depression constant of the solvent, and $m$ is the molality of the solution. 

A higher value of $\Delta T_{f}$ means a greater depression in the freezing point, which results in the lowest freezing point for that solution. Since the mass of the solute is given as $180\text{g}$ in all the options, we can compare the number of moles ($n$) and the effective moles ($i\times n$) for each case.

First, let us find the number of moles of each solute using their molar masses:

Molar mass of acetic acid ($\text{CH}_{3}\text{COOH}$) = $60\text{g mol}^{-1}$

$\text{Moles of acetic acid}=\frac{180\text{g}}{60\text{g mol}^{-1}}=3\text{moles}$

Molar mass of benzoic acid ($\text{C}_{6}\text{H}_{5}\text{COOH}$) = $122\text{g mol}^{-1}$

$\text{Moles of benzoic acid}=\frac{180\text{g}}{122\text{g mol}^{-1}}\approx 1.48\text{moles}$

Molar mass of glucose ($\text{C}_{6}\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_{6}$) = $180\text{g mol}^{-1}$

$\text{Moles of glucose}=\frac{180\text{g}}{180\text{g mol}^{-1}}=1\text{mole}$

Now, let us look at how these solutes behave in their respective solvents to understand the van 't Hoff factor ($i$).

First, let us compare the aqueous solutions (Options B and D), where water is the solvent:

In Option D, glucose is a non-electrolyte, so it does not dissociate in water ($i=1$). The effective number of moles of particles is $1\times 1=1\text{mole}$.

In Option B, acetic acid is a weak electrolyte and dissociates partially in water into $\text{CH}_{3}\text{COO}^{-}$ and $\text{H}^{+}$ ions. Because of this dissociation, $i>1$. Since we already have $3\text{moles}$ of acetic acid, the effective number of moles of particles is greater than $3$. 

Clearly, between the two water solutions, Option B has more particles and will show a much higher depression in freezing point than Option D.

Next, let us compare the benzene solutions (Options A and C):

In benzene, which is a non-polar solvent, both acetic acid and benzoic acid undergo association (dimerisation) due to hydrogen bonding. This makes their van 't Hoff factor $i\approx 0.5$.

For Option A, the effective moles of particles will be roughly $3\times 0.5=1.5\text{moles}$.

For Option C, the effective moles of particles will be roughly $1.48\times 0.5=0.74\text{moles}$.

Even though the $K_{f}$ value for benzene ($5.12\text{K kg mol}^{-1}$) is higher than that of water ($1.86\text{K kg mol}^{-1}$), in standard NCERT problems of this type, the comparison is primarily based on the maximum number of solute particles produced in the solution. 

Since $180\text{g}$ of acetic acid in water gives the highest number of moles ($3\text{moles}$) and further dissociates to give even more particles ($i>1$), it will cause the highest depression in freezing point and therefore have the lowest freezing point.

Thus, the correct option is Option B.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Evening Shift

text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement - I: Since Fluorine is more electronegative than nitrogen, the net dipole moment of $\mathrm{NF}_{3}$ is greater than $\mathrm{NH}_{3}$.

Statement - II: In $\mathrm{NH}_{3}$, the orbital dipole due to lone pair and the dipole moment of $\mathrm{NH}$ bonds are in opposite direction, but in $\mathrm{NF}_{3}$ the orbital dipole due to lone pair and dipole moments of N-F bonds are in same direction.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate from the options given below:
options: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Statement I is false: although fluorine is more electronegative than nitrogen, the dipole moment of $\mathrm{NF}{}_{3}$ (0.24 D) is much smaller than that of $\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}$ (1.47 D).

In $\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}$, nitrogen is more electronegative than hydrogen, so the N–H bond dipoles point towards N, in the same direction as the orbital dipole of the lone pair, and the two add.

In $\mathrm{NF}{}_{3}$, the N–F bond dipoles point away from N towards F, opposite to the orbital dipole of the lone pair, and largely cancel it; Statement II states these directions the other way round, so it is false.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Evening Shift

text: The orange colour of $\mathrm{K}_{2}\mathrm{Cr}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{7}$ and purple colour of $\mathrm{KMnO}_{4}$ is due to
options: $\mathrm{d}\to \mathrm{d}$ transitions in $\mathrm{KMnO}_{4}$ and charge transfer transitions in $\mathrm{K}_{2}\mathrm{Cr}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{7}$.
$\mathrm{d}\to \mathrm{d}$ transitions in $\mathrm{K}_{2}\mathrm{Cr}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{7}$ and charge transfer transitions in $\mathrm{KMnO}_{4}$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In $\mathrm{K}{}_{2}\mathrm{Cr}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{7}$, Cr is in the +6 state ($3d^{0}$); in $\mathrm{KMnO}{}_{4}$, Mn is in the +7 state ($3d^{0}$).

With no d electrons, no $d\to d$ transition is possible in either ion.

The colour arises from ligand-to-metal charge transfer: visible light promotes an electron from an oxide ($\mathrm{O}{}^{2-}$) orbital into an empty metal d orbital, giving orange $\mathrm{Cr}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{7}{}^{2-}$ and purple $\mathrm{MnO}{}_{4}{}^{-}$.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Evening Shift

text: The coordination geometry around the manganese in decacarbonyldimanganese $(0)$ is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:

Each Mn is bonded to five CO groups and to the other Mn atom, so it has six bonded neighbours: four CO in a plane, one axial CO, and the Mn–Mn bond trans to that axial CO. This arrangement is octahedral.

The square pyramidal shape describes only the $\mathrm{Mn}(\mathrm{CO}){}_{5}$ fragment; with the Mn–Mn bond included, the coordination geometry around each Mn is octahedral.

text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement - I: Along the period, the chemical reactivity of the elements gradually increases from group 1 to group 18 .

Statement - II: The nature of oxides formed by group 1 elements is basic while that of group 17 elements is acidic.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate from the options given below:
options: Statement I is False but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are False
Statement I is True But Statement II is False
Both Statement I and Statement II are True
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Along a period, chemical reactivity is highest at the two extremes, in the group 1 metals and the group 17 non-metals, and lowest in the middle; the group 18 noble gases are almost unreactive. Reactivity therefore does not increase gradually from group 1 to group 18, so Statement I is false.

Elements at the extreme left of a period form basic oxides (for example $\mathrm{Na}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$), while those at the extreme right form acidic oxides (for example $\mathrm{Cl}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{7}$). Statement II is true.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Evening Shift

text: Number of spectral lines obtained in $\mathrm{He}^{+}$ spectra, when an electron makes transition from fifth excited state to first excited state will be
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The fifth excited state is $n=6$ and the first excited state is $n=2$.

On its way down the electron can stop at any of the levels $n=6,5,4,3,2$, so $N=6-2+1=5$ levels are involved. A sample contains many $\mathrm{He}{}^{+}$ ions, so every pair of these levels gives a line in the spectrum.

$\text{Number of lines}=\dfrac{N(N-1)}{2}=\dfrac{5\times 4}{2}=10$

The lines are $6\to 5$, $6\to 4$, $6\to 3$, $6\to 2$, $5\to 4$, $5\to 3$, $5\to 2$, $4\to 3$, $4\to 2$ and $3\to 2$.

Hence, the answer is 10.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Evening Shift

text:
Total number of species from the following which can undergo disproportionation reaction is $________$.

$\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{2},\mathrm{ClO}_{3}^{-},\mathrm{P}_{4},\mathrm{Cl}_{2},\mathrm{Ag},\mathrm{Cu}^{+1},\mathrm{F}_{2},\mathrm{NO}_{2},\mathrm{K}^{+}$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
A species can disproportionate only when it contains an element in an intermediate oxidation state, so that the element is oxidised and reduced at the same time.

$\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{2}$ (O: $-1$, between $-2$ and $0$): $2~\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{2}\longrightarrow 2\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}+\mathrm{O}{}_{2}$

$\mathrm{ClO}{}_{3}{}^{-}$ (Cl: $+5$, between $-1$ and $+7$): $4~\mathrm{ClO}{}_{3}{}^{-}\longrightarrow \mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}+3\mathrm{ClO}{}_{4}{}^{-}$

$\mathrm{P}{}_{4}$ (P: $0$, between $-3$ and $+5$): $\mathrm{P}{}_{4}+3\mathrm{OH}{}^{-}+3\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}\longrightarrow \mathrm{PH}{}_{3}+3\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{PO}{}_{2}{}^{-}$

$\mathrm{Cl}{}_{2}$ (Cl: $0$, between $-1$ and $+1$): $\mathrm{Cl}{}_{2}+2\mathrm{OH}{}^{-}\longrightarrow \mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}+\mathrm{ClO}{}^{-}+\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$

$\mathrm{Cu}{}^{+}$ ($+1$, between $0$ and $+2$): $2~\mathrm{Cu}{}^{+}\longrightarrow \mathrm{Cu}+\mathrm{Cu}{}^{2+}$

$\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}$ (N: $+4$, between $+3$ and $+5$): $2~\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}+\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}\longrightarrow \mathrm{HNO}{}_{2}+\mathrm{HNO}{}_{3}$

Ag ($0$) is in its lowest and $\mathrm{K}{}^{+}$ ($+1$) in its highest oxidation state. Fluorine shows only $0$ and $-1$, so in $2~\mathrm{F}{}_{2}+2\mathrm{OH}{}^{-}\longrightarrow 2\mathrm{F}{}^{-}+\mathrm{OF}{}_{2}+\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ fluorine is only reduced while oxygen is oxidised; this is not disproportionation.

The six species are $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{2}$, $\mathrm{ClO}{}_{3}{}^{-}$, $\mathrm{P}{}_{4}$, $\mathrm{Cl}{}_{2}$, $\mathrm{Cu}{}^{+}$ and $\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}$.

Hence, the answer is 6.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Evening Shift

text:
Number of geometrical isomers possible for the given structure is/are $_________$.


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The structure is $\mathrm{DHC}=\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3})-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{C}(=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{3})-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3})=\mathrm{CHD}$, constitutionally symmetric about the central carbon.

Each terminal $\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{CHD}$ bond has two different groups on each carbon (H and D; $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ and $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{R}$), so each is stereogenic (E or Z).

The central carbon of $\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ carries two $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3})=\mathrm{CHD}$ arms, which are identical when both terminal bonds have the same configuration and different when the configurations differ.

Terminal E,E: the central bond is not stereogenic, giving 1 isomer. Terminal Z,Z: likewise 1 isomer.

Terminal E,Z (identical to Z,E by symmetry): the central $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ can lie on the side of the E-arm or of the Z-arm, giving 2 isomers.

Total geometrical isomers $=1+1+2=4$.

Hence, the answer is 4.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Evening Shift

text: The $\mathrm{pH}$ of an aqueous solution containing $1\mathrm{M}$ benzoic acid $(\mathrm{pK}_{\mathrm{a}}=4.20)$ and $1\mathrm{M}$ sodium benzoate is 4.5. The volume of benzoic acid solution in $300\mathrm{mL}$ of this buffer solution is $_________$ $\mathrm{mL}$. (given : $\log 2=0.3$)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{lll}  & \text{1M Benzoic acid} & +1\mathrm{M}\text{Sodium Benzoate} \\  & (\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{a}}\mathrm{ml}) & (\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{s}}\mathrm{ml}) \\ \text{Millimole} & \mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{a}}\times 1 & \mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{s}}\times 1 \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{pH}=4.5 \\ \mathrm{pH}=\mathrm{pka}+\log \dfrac{[\text{salt}]}{[\text{acid}]} \\ 4.5=4.2+\log \left (\dfrac{\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{s}}}{\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{a}}}\right ) \\ \dfrac{\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{s}}}{\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{a}}}=2\text{..... (1)} \\ \mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{s}}+\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{a}}=300\text{..... (2)} \\ \mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{a}}=100\mathrm{ml} \end{array}$

text:
$\mathrm{NO}_{2}$ required for a reaction is produced by decomposition of $\mathrm{N}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{5}$ in $\mathrm{CCl}_{4}$ as by equation

$2\mathrm{N}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{5(\mathrm{g})}\to 4\mathrm{NO}_{2(\mathrm{g})}+\mathrm{O}_{2(\mathrm{g})}$

The initial concentration of $\mathrm{N}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{5}$ is $3\mathrm{mol}\mathrm{L}^{-1}$ and it is $2.75\mathrm{mol}\mathrm{L}^{-1}$ after 30 minutes.

The rate of formation of $\mathrm{NO}_{2}$ is $\mathrm{x}\times 10^{-3}\mathrm{mol}\mathrm{L}^{-1}\min ^{-1}$, value of $\mathrm{x}$ is $_________. ($nearest integer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Rate of reaction (ROR)

$\begin{array}{l} =-\dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{\Delta [\mathrm{N}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{5}]}{\Delta \mathrm{t}}=\dfrac{1}{4}\dfrac{\Delta [\mathrm{NO}_{2}]}{\Delta \mathrm{t}}=\dfrac{\Delta [\mathrm{O}_{2}]}{\Delta \mathrm{t}} \\ \mathrm{ROR}=-\dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{\Delta [\mathrm{N}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{5}]}{\Delta \mathrm{t}}=-\dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{(2.75-3)}{30}\mathrm{mol}\mathrm{L}^{-1}\min ^{-1} \\ \mathrm{ROR}=-\dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{(-0.25)}{30}\mathrm{mol}\mathrm{L}^{-1}\min ^{-1} \\ \text{ROR}=\dfrac{1}{240}\mathrm{mol}\mathrm{L}^{-1}\min ^{-1} \end{array}$

Rate of formation of $\mathrm{NO}_{2}=\frac{\Delta [\mathrm{NO}_{2}]}{\Delta \mathrm{t}}=4\times \mathrm{ROR}$

$=\frac{4}{240}=16.66\times 10^{-3}\mathrm{molL}^{-1}\min ^{-1}\simeq 17\times 10^{-3}\text{.}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Evening Shift

text:
Number of complexes which show optical isomerism among the following is $________$.

$\text{cis-}[\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{ox})_{2}\mathrm{Cl}_{2}]^{3-},[\mathrm{Co}(\text{en})_{3}]^{3+},\text{cis-}[\mathrm{Pt}(\text{en})_{2}\mathrm{Cl}_{2}]^{2+},\text{cis-}[\mathrm{Co}(\text{en})_{2}\mathrm{Cl}_{2}]^{+},\text{trans-}[\mathrm{Pt}(\text{en})_{2}\mathrm{Cl}_{2}]^{2+},\text{trans-}[\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{ox})_{2}\mathrm{Cl}_{2}]^{3-}$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
A complex is optically active when it has neither a plane nor a centre of symmetry.

cis-$[\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{ox}){}_{2}\mathrm{Cl}{}_{2}]{}^{3-}$, cis-$[\mathrm{Pt}(\mathrm{en}){}_{2}\mathrm{Cl}{}_{2}]{}^{2+}$ and cis-$[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{en}){}_{2}\mathrm{Cl}{}_{2}]{}^{+}$ are octahedral cis-$[\mathrm{M}(\mathrm{AA}){}_{2}\mathrm{B}{}_{2}]$ species: the two chelate rings lie in different planes and the two $\mathrm{Cl}$ atoms are adjacent, so there is no plane or centre of symmetry and each exists as a pair of enantiomers.

$[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{en}){}_{3}]{}^{3+}$ is an $[\mathrm{M}(\mathrm{AA}){}_{3}]$ species with non-superimposable $\Delta$ and $\Lambda$ forms, so it is optically active.

In trans-$[\mathrm{Pt}(\mathrm{en}){}_{2}\mathrm{Cl}{}_{2}]{}^{2+}$ and trans-$[\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{ox}){}_{2}\mathrm{Cl}{}_{2}]{}^{3-}$, both chelate rings lie in one plane, which is a plane of symmetry, and the metal is a centre of symmetry, so both are optically inactive.

Number of complexes showing optical isomerism $=4$.

Hence, the answer is 4.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Evening Shift

text:
2-chlorobutane $+\mathrm{Cl}_{2}\to \mathrm{C}_{4}\mathrm{H}_{8}\mathrm{Cl}_{2}$ (isomers)

Total number of optically active isomers shown by $\mathrm{C}_{4}\mathrm{H}_{8}\mathrm{Cl}_{2}$, obtained in the above reaction is $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Free-radical chlorination ($\mathrm{Cl}{}_{2}/hν$) of 2-chlorobutane, $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}-\mathrm{CHCl}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$, replaces one H atom at C1, C2, C3 or C4, giving four structural isomers of $\mathrm{C}{}_{4}\mathrm{H}{}_{8}\mathrm{Cl}{}_{2}$.

At C1: $\mathrm{ClCH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{CHCl}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ (1,2-dichlorobutane) has one chiral carbon (C2), so it exists as 2 optically active enantiomers.

At C2: $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}-\mathrm{CCl}{}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ (2,2-dichlorobutane) has no chiral carbon and is optically inactive.

At C3: $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}-\mathrm{CHCl}-\mathrm{CHCl}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ (2,3-dichlorobutane) has two similar chiral carbons; the (2R,3R) and (2S,3S) forms are optically active, while the (2R,3S) form is meso and inactive, giving 2 optically active isomers.

At C4: $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}-\mathrm{CHCl}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{Cl}$ (1,3-dichlorobutane) has one chiral carbon (C3), so it exists as 2 optically active enantiomers.

Total optically active isomers $=2+0+2+2=6$.

Hence, the answer is 6.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Evening Shift

text:
Two reactions are given below:

$\begin{array}{l} 2\mathrm{Fe}_{(\mathrm{s})}+\dfrac{3}{2}\mathrm{O}_{2(\mathrm{g})}\to \mathrm{Fe}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3(\mathrm{s})},\Delta \mathrm{H}^{\circ }=-822\mathrm{kJ}/\mathrm{mol} \\ \mathrm{C}_{(\mathrm{s})}+\dfrac{1}{2}\mathrm{O}_{2(\mathrm{g})}\to \mathrm{CO}_{(\mathrm{g})},\Delta \mathrm{H}^{\circ }=-110\mathrm{kJ}/\mathrm{mol} \end{array}$

Then enthalpy change for following reaction $3\mathrm{C}_{(\mathrm{s})}+\mathrm{Fe}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3(\mathrm{s})}\to 2\mathrm{Fe}_{(\mathrm{s})}+3\mathrm{CO}_{(\mathrm{g})}$ is $_______$ $\mathrm{kJ}/\mathrm{mol}$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$2\mathrm{Fe}_{(\mathrm{s})}+\frac{3}{2}\mathrm{O}_{2(\mathrm{g})}\to \mathrm{Fe}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3(\mathrm{s})},\Delta \mathrm{H}^{\circ }=-822\mathrm{kJ}/\mathrm{mol}$ ........ (1)

$\mathrm{C}_{(\mathrm{s})}+\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{O}_{2(\mathrm{g})}\to \mathrm{CO}_{(\mathrm{g})},\Delta \mathrm{H}^{\circ }=-110\mathrm{kJ}/\mathrm{mol}$ ........ (2)

$3\mathrm{C}_{(\mathrm{s})}+\mathrm{Fe}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3(\mathrm{s})}\to 2\mathrm{Fe}_{(\mathrm{s})}+3\mathrm{CO}_{(\mathrm{g})},\Delta \mathrm{H}_{3}=\text{?}$

$\begin{array}{ll} (3)=3\times (2)-(1) \\ \begin{array}{ll} \Delta \mathrm{H}_{3} & =3\times \Delta \mathrm{H}_{2}-\Delta \mathrm{H}_{1} \\ \qquad =3(-110)+822 \\ \qquad =492\mathrm{kJ}/\mathrm{mole} \end{array} \end{array}$
